questions.question: Select the sentence with no spelling errors.

options.text: I had to play melody while simultaneously playing harmony with him.
I had to play melody while simultaneously playing harmuny with him.
I had to play melodie while simultaneously playing harmony with him.
I had to play melody while simultanously playing harmony with him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **I had to play melody while simultaneously playing harmony with him**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"melody"** refers to a sequence of musical notes that are perceived as a single entity; it is the main theme of a piece of music. (मधुर धुन)

 
 
• **Example: **The melody of the song was so catchy that everyone started humming along.
 
 
 
• **"Harmony"** refers to the combination of simultaneously sounded musical notes to produce a pleasing effect. (संगति)
 
 
• **Example: **The choir's voices blended in perfect harmony.
 
 
 
• Only in **option 1**, all the spellings are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. I had to play melody while simultaneously playing harmony with him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **harmuny** is a misspelling of the word **"harmony."**
 
• **melodie** is a misspelling of the word **"melody."**
 
• **simultanously** is a misspelling of the word **"simultaneously."**

My puns are usually greeted ________ loud applause by my friends.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **with**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition** 'with' **is used to indicate association or accompaniment.

 
 
• For example: The president was greeted with a huge round of applause.
 
 
 
• The phrase** 'greeted with loud applause'** is a common English expression.
 
• The other prepositions ('against', 'to', 'for') don't fit contextually in this sentence.
 
• Using** 'with'** properly conveys that the puns are met or accompanied by loud applause.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'with'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Example: "The protest was against the new law."
 
 
 
• **To: **This preposition is often used to indicate direction or destination.
 
 
• Example: "She went to the market."
 
 
 
• **For: **This preposition is generally used to indicate the purpose or reason.
 
 
• Example: "He went there for a meeting."

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I __meet an homeless__ person in New York.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **met a homeless**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb tense **'meet'** is incorrect for this **past event.**
 
• **'met' **is required for **past tense** agreement.
 
• The article **'an'** is incorrect before **'homeless'.**
 
• **'a' **should be used because **'homeless'** starts with a **consonant sound**.
 
• The sentence describes an event that has already happened; hence, past tense 'met' is appropriate.

The corrected sentence should be: *"I **met a homeless** person in New York."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Met an homeless:** Incorrect due to the misuse of the article 'an' before a word beginning with a consonant sound.
 
• **Will met a homeless:** Incorrect use of future tense auxiliary 'will' with the past form 'met'; it should be 'will meet' for future tense but this does not fit the context of a past event.
 
• **No improvement:** Incorrect, as the original sentence contains errors in verb tense and article usage.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Mansa is not _________ than Mamta.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **'taller'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase** 'not ___ than'** indicates a **comparative form** is needed.
 
• The comparative form of an adjective is used to compare two nouns and typically ends in "-er" or uses the word "more" before the adjective, depending on the word length and spelling rules.
 
• The comparative form of 'tall' is **'taller'**.
 
• The context tells us that Mamta and Mansa are comparable in height.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'taller'**.

Hence, the corrected sentence is: *Mansa is not **taller **than Mamta*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tallest: **This is a superlative adjective used when comparing more than two entities. It does not fit in a comparative context.
 
• **Tall: **This is the positive form of the adjective and does not indicate a comparison.
 
• **More taller: **This is an incorrect comparative form because 'taller' itself is a comparative. Adding 'more' is redundant and grammatically incorrect.

• **Example:** *The teacher has **explained** the lesson.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'encouraged' instead of 'encourage'.

• In the present perfect tense, the auxiliary verb **'has'** or **'have'** is always followed by the past participle form of the main verb.

 
 
• **Example:** *She has **finished** her homework.*
 
 
 
• Common mistakes include using the base form of the verb instead of the past participle.
 
 
• Example: *Incorrect: He has **go** to the store.

 Correct: He has **gone** to the store.*
